title: ‘Paper Tiger’ Producer Rodrigo Teixeira Set for GLAFF’s First Visionary Award, Presented by Wagner Moura (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Two-time Oscar-nominated producer Rodrigo Teixeira will receive the inaugural Árbol de la Vida Visionary Award at the GuadaLAjara Film Festival (GL
body:
Two-time Oscar-nominated producer Rodrigo Teixeira will receive the inaugural Árbol de la Vida Visionary Award at the GuadaLAjara Film Festival (GLAFF), the Los Angeles offshoot of the Guadalajara International Film Festival, on Nov. 6.

	The honor will be presented by Oscar-nominated actor Wagner Moura ahead of a screening of James Gray’s “Paper Tiger,” which Teixeira produced. The award recognizes individuals who have made a lasting impact on cinema and strengthened the ties between Latin America and the international film industry.
	

	Teixeira will also serve as the first mentor of the GLAFF Co-Production Lab, a new industry initiative developed with the Guadalajara International Film Festival (FICG) to foster co-productions between Mexico and the United States.


	“Rodrigo Teixeira has built a career defined by bold storytelling and a true commitment to artists across the border,” says Ximena Urrutia, executive director of GLAFF. “As inaugural mentor of our New Mexico-U. S. co-production lab, he will help emerging filmmakers turn ambitious cross-border projects into lasting partnerships.”

	For more than two decades, Teixeira has bridged Latin American and global filmmaking through his production company RT Features, whose credits include “Call Me by Your Name,” “The Lighthouse,” “The Witch” and “Invisible Life.” He earned best picture nominations for “Call Me by Your Name” and Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here,” which won the Oscar for international feature. Films from his banner have collected nine Oscar nominations and six Golden Globe nominations.
	

	“Paper Tiger” marks the third collaboration between Teixeira and Gray, following “Ad Astra” and “Armageddon Time.”

	The 16th edition of GLAFF runs Nov. 5-7 in Los Angeles, opening with Diego Luna’s “Ashes” and closing with Eddie Sánchez’s “Mexicanamerican.”

schema.headline: ‘Paper Tiger’ Producer Rodrigo Teixeira Set for GLAFF’s First Visionary Award, Presented by Wagner Moura (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Poison Ivy DC Series in the Works at HBO With ‘The Penguin’ Exec Lauren LeFranc
description:
Another Batman villain may be getting their own TV series.

	A Poison Ivy TV show is in the works at HBO with “The Penguin” showrunner Lauren LeFra
body:
Another Batman villain may be getting their own TV series.

	A Poison Ivy TV show is in the works at HBO with “The Penguin” showrunner Lauren LeFranc as a producer, Variety has confirmed.

	LeFranc’s “The Penguin” marked the first live-action spinoff from a Batman movie, after Colin Farrell originated his villain in Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” in 2022. It aired on HBO in 2024 and became a hit with critics and fans for its gritty, gangster story. Farrell won an Emmy and Golden Globe for his lead performance, and the show nabbed several best limited series nominations.
	

	Poison Ivy, the green femme fatale from the Batman comics, has never been the main focus of a movie or TV show, but she’s appeared in several live-action and animated DC titles. The classic villain has the ability to control plants and often controls people’s minds using seductive pheromones. She first arrived on the big screen in 1997’s “Batman & Robin” and was played by Uma Thurman. In live-action TV, she also appeared in “Gotham” and “Batwoman,” and she’s popped up in several animated shows like “Batman: The Brave and the Bold,” “The New Batman Adventures,” “Young Justice” and more. Recently, she was voiced by Lake Bell in “Harley Quinn” and played the titular character’s girlfriend.


	The DC Universe is expanding this weekend with “Clayface,” focused on the shape-shifting Batman villain. It’s unconnected to Robert Pattinson and Reeves’ world, which is continuing in 2028 with “The Batman Part 2.” HBO will also air “The People vs. Gorilla Grodd,” a comedic, villain-focused spinoff from James Gunn’s “Superman” movie, sometime in 2027.

schema.headline: Poison Ivy DC Series in the Works at HBO With ‘The Penguin’ Exec Lauren LeFranc

title: ‘ComicView: Rooftop Series’ Renewed for Season 2 at BET (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Keep on laughing: BET’s “ComicView” reboot has been renewed for Season 2.

	BET has ordered 20 more episodes of the revived stand-up franchise, whi
body:
Keep on laughing: BET’s “ComicView” reboot has been renewed for Season 2.

	BET has ordered 20 more episodes of the revived stand-up franchise, which premiered in June as “ComicView: Rooftop Series.” Chris “CP” Powell returns as host of the program, which will see 60 comedians performing on a Hollywood rooftop.

	Veteran comics Affion Crockett, Cocoa Brown, Lavell Crawford and Luenell join the Season 2 lineup alongside rising talent.
	

	“I’m beyond proud and excited to be back at the helm for Season 2 of ‘ComicView: Rooftop Series,’” Powell said. “Season 1 was amazing, and this season promises to be even better, with bigger comics and even bigger laughs. BET being back at the forefront of stand-up comedy just feels right!”


	“ComicView” first aired in 1992 as a nationally broadcast showcase for up-and-coming comics. The show became a pillar of Black comedy and a launchpad for talent that would go on to become huge names in stand-up, including D.L. Hughley, Sommore, Cedric the Entertainer and Bruce Bruce.

	The series rotated hosts throughout its initial run from 1992 to 2008, and it was briefly revived in 2014. After a nine-year absence, the show returned in 2024 as a four-episode series hosted by Mike Epps, taped at Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat Weekend in Las Vegas.

	“‘ComicView’ is part of BET’s DNA, and this rooftop proved our audience is still hungry for it,” said Aisha Summers-Burke, EVP, head of creative, BET Studios. “Season 2 puts a whole new class of comics in front of them, and there’s no one better than CP to hand them the mic.”
	

	“ComicView: Rooftop Series” is executive produced by Jeru Tillman for Southfield Village Entertainment.

schema.headline: ‘ComicView: Rooftop Series’ Renewed for Season 2 at BET (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Meta’s Almost $10 Billion Legal Costs Take Huge Toll on Q3 Earnings, Wall Street Shrugs
description: Meta’s $18 billion nationwide settlement with state attorneys general forced nearly $10 billion in additional costs for the company during its thir
body:
Meta’s $18 billion nationwide settlement with state attorneys general forced nearly $10 billion in additional costs for the company during its third quarter in 2026, missing Wall Street expectations on per-share earnings Wednesday even as its quarterly revenue was up 28%.

	The company’s revenue for the quarter hit $64.6 billion, up 26%, while its net income was $9.86 billion, up 264%. Its earnings per share hit $3.83. Analysts polled by LSEG Data & Analytics expected the company’s revenue to hit $63.4 billion and earnings per share of $5.46. 
	

	Wall Street analysts didn’t seem to mind the lower EPS, however, as its share price was up 5% after market close. The company also unveiled plans to create a new class of non-voting Class C common stock starting in January.


	“We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone – including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model,” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in a statement. “Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we’re seeing velocity across the board.”

	The earnings report came hours after a New Mexico state judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company liable last month for deceiving users about Facebook‘s data privacy and content moderation policies. That ruling came after Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with 52 state attorneys general in August over claims that it designed Instagram with addictive features, knowingly exposed young users to serious mental harms, and intentionally misled the public about the safety of its platforms, among other claims.
	

	The settlement saw Meta’s costs for the quarter balloon to $51.6 billion. The company said in its earnings release that its operating income would have jumped from $12.98 billion to $22.88 billion — had it not had $9.89 billion in costs from the settlement.

	Meta’s third quarter saw the company effectively relaunch its AI efforts, including the introduction of its AI agent Muse, a Muse-infused gadget and a new suite of Meta-branded eyeglasses.

	“I am proud of what we are building,” Zuckerberg said during the company’s earnings call on Wednesday. “People have all kinds of different opinions about the future, but at Meta, we believe that the future is for everyone and that putting power in people’s hands is how we get there. I think that this matters. There needs to be a company out there that represents these ideas, but this isn’t just about ideas; it’s also about execution.”

	Meta introduced Muse last month, touting the agent as “the world’s first personal AI agent built for everyone.” The agent took center stage at its Meta Connect event last month, where it was given both an animated character to represent it and an infusion into several of the company’s software and hardware offerings. During the company’s earnings call, Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse agents, and 25% of those who set up agents use Muse daily. Its most common use cases include shopping, personal productivity and creativity, chief financial office Susan Li revealed.

	“We want to help every person have an extremely capable personal agent that understands your goals and can help you achieve them and improve your life in whatever ways you want, whether that’s improving your relationships, helping you save time, save money, build a business, create new things, or anything else that you can dream of,” Zuckerberg said. “Muse is the product form of this vision. So now we have the foundational technology in place to deliver this. There is still a lot of work ahead, but our initial position is very strong.”

	AI remained a hot topic throughout the earnings call, with analysts peppering Zuckerberg and Li with questions about the company’s AI strategy. Meta has made enterprise and subscriptions pillars of its AI focus, the executives shared, while also building out new components of its AI products.
	

	“The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage,” Li said. “And beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services, we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents.”

	Ultimately, the goal is to produce some level of a “personal superintelligence,” a company ethos Zuckerberg debuted in an essay last year and reiterated repeatedly on the call Wednesday as Meta aims to create a large-scale “Muse network.”

	“We believe in putting the power of personal superintelligence in everyone’s hands,” he said. “We believe that that is the path to ensuring a positive future for everyone, with individual empowerment as the source of prosperity and balance of power as the foundation for safety. On a values level, we believe that delivering this capability widely is the best thing that we can be doing. This is also our strategy because we think that billions of muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together.”

schema.headline: Meta’s Almost $10 Billion Legal Costs Take Huge Toll on Q3 Earnings, Wall Street Shrugs

title: Alexander Skarsgård on His Wacky ‘Wicker’ Red Carpet Looks: From Clear Shoes and a Multicolored Skirt to a Gray Wig Inspired by Co-Star Olivia Colman
description:
Alexander Skarsgård knows how to make an entrance.

	The Swedish actor has been turning heads with his wacky red carpet looks while promoting his n
body:
Alexander Skarsgård knows how to make an entrance.

	The Swedish actor has been turning heads with his wacky red carpet looks while promoting his new fantasy romance “Wicker.”

	At the London premiere earlier this month, he donned a metallic gold Saint Laurent suit. If that wasn’t bold enough, he slipped into a pair of clear plastic lace-up shoes.


	“They were surprisingly comfortable, and I was worried that they would steam up in five minutes, but that actually didn’t happen,” Skarsgård told me Saturday at the Academy Museum Gala. “But I’ve been getting a lot of comments from friends and family about my little piglets sticking out. They make fun of me. They make fun of my feet.”
	


	At the “Wicker” premiere in Los Angeles on Tuesday, Skarsgård wore a multicolored skirt and a whimsical black shirt adorned with his co-star Olivia Colman’s face from London fashion house Chopova Lowena. “We’ve been on a press tour for a couple of weeks, and now we’re in L.A., and it’s our final big premiere before the movie opens on Friday,” he said. “I wanted to wear something special for this lovely lady over here, Olivia, whom I adore.”

	As for the purple and green skirt, Skarsgård said, “It’s very comfortable. It’s quite a hot night, and it’s light and breezy. I’m enjoying it.”

	Earlier in the day, he shocked attendees at a SAG-AFTRA screening and Q&A when he arrived in a long gray wig. “I got a little jealous because everyone is complimenting Olivia on her beautiful hair and beautiful hair color,” Skarsgård said. “I got no love for my hair. As a narcissistic actor, I need a little bit of attention, so I threw on a beautiful gray wig to match Olivia today.”
	

	“Wicker” co-star Elizabeth Debicki praised Skarsgård’s fashion choices. “He can do no wrong,” she said. “I love the man. What can I say? I’m biased.”

	In “Wicker,” Colman plays an outcast in a medieval town who falls in love with a man made of wicker (Skarsgård). Debicki plays a housewife who burns with jealousy over the attention the townspeople give to Colman and Skarsgård’s characters.

	Skarsgård’s wicker look was a practical costume created by the Wētā Workshop in New Zealand, with lead makeup effects artist Sarah Rubano, prosthetic designer Joe Dunckley and lead weaver Jasmin van Lith.

	“Amazing,” Colman said of seeing Skarsgård in the costume for the first time. “We’d seen backward and forwards from Weta Workshop in New Zealand images for about 18 months, and so suddenly he puts it on, and we were all going, ‘Oh God, I hope it works.’ And he came out of the makeup trailer and went, ‘Oh God, it’s beautiful.’”


	“Wicker” is in limited release starting Oct. 23 before expanding on Oct. 30.

schema.headline: Alexander Skarsgård on His Wacky ‘Wicker’ Red Carpet Looks: From Clear Shoes and a Multicolored Skirt to a Gray Wig Inspired by Co-Star Olivia Colman

title: Brandi Carlile to Receive Humanitarian Honor at National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards
description: Brandi Carlile will be the recipient of the Los Angeles Press Club‘s annual Visionary Award for Humanitarian Work, to be given out at the National
body:
Brandi Carlile will be the recipient of the Los Angeles Press Club‘s annual Visionary Award for Humanitarian Work, to be given out at the National Arts and Entertainment Journalism Awards Gala in December, the organization has announced.

	Carlile’s honor will be part of the dinner and awards show that takes place Dec. 6 at downtown L.A.’s Millennium Biltmore. About 800 working journalists and guests gather in the historic Crystal Ballroom for a night in which competitive awards are given out to reporters, critics and photographers covering the arts, along with a handful of lifetime achievement honors for major arts figures as well as journalists.
	

	Also set to be celebrated that night is KCRW’s Madeleine Brand, who will receive the Luminary Award for Career Achievement in Media. Brand has hosted the popular “Press Play” for the station since 2014 and has worked in the public radio sphere for more than 30 years. Other honorees will be announced in the days to come, the Press Club said.


	The Visionary Award was first given out at the National A&E Journalism Awards Gala in 2012, to Jane Fonda, with Robert Redford presenting it to her. Last year, it went to Seth Rogan and Lauren Miller Rogen in honor of their charitable work. Others who have received it over the years include Quincy Jones, Tiffany Haddish, Diane Warren and Forest Whitaker.

	“We are excited to have Brandi Carlile as this year’s Visionary Awardee,” said Los Angeles Press Club President Danny Bakewell, Jr. “Her work is amazing and, during these troubling times, desperately needed. Topical songs like ‘The Joke,’ ‘Human’ and ‘Church & State’ have spoken to her vision for social justice, as well as providing a showcase for one of the great voices in contemporary music. Her eagerness to reach out has led her to collaborate closely with figures like Elton John and Joni Mitchell, but that spirit isn’t just reserved for her heroes; it’s her compassion for society’s underdogs that has most touched millions of listeners.”
	

	Earlier in October, Carlile appeared at the Grammy Museum in L.A. for a conversation with Cameron Crowe and a full-band performance to mark the one-year anniversary of her eighth studio album, “Returning to Myself.” She just released a deluxe companion version of the album with all of the original tracks reimagined in stripped-down arrangements, archly titled “Returning to Myself (Sad Gay Version).” Carlile and her longtime band members Phil and Tim Hanseroth recently wrapped up their first headlining tour in U.S. arenas, named the “Human Tour” after one of the key songs on the latest album. In November, they will briefly move back into theaters for the immediately sold-out tour dubbed “Burn the Setlist (The All-Request Tour)” before resuming the “Human Tour” in Europe in early 2027.

	On the philanthropic side, Carlile has dedicated a portion of her ticket sales to fund her grassroots organization, the Looking Out Foundation, which has granted more than $10 million to community-based nonprofit organizations working to support humanitarian causes across the globe. Carlile has bolstered these efforts through the creation of her wine club, XOBC Cellars, which was created in part to send proceeds to the Looking Out Foundation, “helping them to defend the rights and joys of refugees, immigrants, the LGBTQIA2S+ community and more.” Early in the “Human Tour,” she livestreamed “Be Human: A Concert for Minneapolis” (now viewable on YouTube), which raised over $750,000 for Minnesota’s The Advocates for Human Rights to help families and individuals affected by ICE.

schema.headline: Brandi Carlile to Receive Humanitarian Honor at National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards

title: Olivia Cooke on Returning to ‘Slow Horses,’ On-Set Injuries and That Shocking Finale Cliffhanger: ‘I Want a Showdown!’
description: SPOILER ALERT: The following article contains plot details from “Judgement Day,” the Season 6 finale of “Slow Horses,” now streaming on Apple TV.
body:
SPOILER ALERT: The following article contains plot details from “Judgement Day,” the Season 6 finale of “Slow Horses,” now streaming on Apple TV.

	“Hello, River.”

	Those two fateful words announced Olivia Cooke’s return to “Slow Horses” after a four-season absence from the Apple TV spy drama. Cooke’s MI5 agent Sidonie Baker made a brief but memorable appearance in Season 1, forging a flirty chemistry with inept spy River Cartwright (Jack Lowden) before dying from a gunshot wound to the head — or so River thinks.
	

	Sid’s resurrection wasn’t a total surprise to “Slow Horses” fans: the character comes back in author Mick Herron’s namesake novels, and Apple made little secret of her storyline in the advance promotion for Season 6, which concluded this week. But enough has changed since Cooke’s first stint on the show to make her re-joining the ensemble an event in itself. First, “Slow Horses” itself grew into a hit, with a raft of Emmy nominations (plus a few wins) and an avid audience to show for it; meanwhile, Cooke’s own career has taken off thanks to a leading role in the fantasy epic “House of the Dragon.”


	That star power is on full display throughout Season 6, which sees Sid and River on the run from Russian sleeper agents over one incredibly stressful night. Icy MI5 head Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas) — who once planted her favored mentee Sid in Slough House, a kind of purgatory for screwup agents, as her eyes and ears — used Sid’s identity as a cover for an off-the-books assassination on Russian soil, and now the Kremlin is out for revenge. All of the Slow Horses (a not-so-affectionate nickname for Slough House employees), past and present, are targeted, and Sid goes to River for help.
	

	The pair’s winding route from River’s late grandfather’s country house to Diana’s beach retreat, which Slough House head Jackson Lamb (Gary Oldman) cheekily appropriates as a safe house, is a winding one. Sid and River barrel through a barn, an arcade, and finally an airstrip where Sid is nearly shipped off to Russia as an unwilling sacrifice on their way to a long-awaited first kiss. This being “Slow Horses,” though, their triumph is short-lived: River helps Sid escape and nearly reunites with her at his grandfather’s house, but collapses from an apparent poisoning in the kitchen while she showers upstairs in the season’s final moments.

	“River has kept her going, in a sense,” Cooke says now of the star-crossed lovers. Speaking with Variety from the U.K., the actor shared what it’s been like to dive back into the deep end with over a month of night shoots, from an unlikely injury to her collaboration with Lowden. 



	

									Courtesy of Apple TV
	


	
		Your character comes back in the books, but I’m sure when you were first filming, it wasn’t certain we would get to this point. Did you know there was a chance you would return?	

	We shot [Season 1] towards the end of 2020. It was one of the first projects back after lockdown. I don’t know if the book had come out yet where I make my return, but there were whispers of it. I don’t know. It was such an uncertain time, and it was the first series as well. It just felt, like, an eon away. Who would have thought it would have gone on for so long?

	But they kept me abreast of all the things that were going on story-wise over the years. I’ve been admiring from afar, and biding my time. I’d get messages from Jack being like, “You’re coming back!” and I’m like, “Fantastic, when?” And no one could really give me a clear answer. I remember seeing Saskia [Reeves], who plays Standish, at the theater, and she was like, “You coming back? And I was like, “I would love to. I just don’t know. I have no clear answers.” We were all just in a cloud of mystery for a bit.
	
		During that time, what was it like for you to watch this show that you were once a part of, but weren’t for a while?	

	Really fun, but tinged with jealousy. Because I experienced it, you know? Even though we were all masked up and socially distanced from each other and the crew when we weren’t in the scenes, it was such a fun, charmed environment that I was just desperate to get back to. And it’s so palpable — watching Season 2, 3, 4, 5 — just how much fun everyone’s having on set. It really just glows through the screen. So it’s always bittersweet. I love watching them, and I love seeing how good all my friends are, but I’m also incredibly jealous as well that they’re all having fun without me.
	
	
		I imagine that, as an actor, having to return to a character that you left behind is a challenge. Is there any work or preparation that you did to reassume this role?	

	I had to remind myself how I sounded, like what accent I was doing. I had to check back in with that. But also, it was quite nice, because Sid is coming back in a very jaded way. Both her and River have grown up mentally in the interim. They’ve been away from each other, and the events that led up to Sid’s disappearance were really traumatic. So I had a bit of rope to not honor the more jovial, happy-go-lucky version of Sid that we saw in the first season.
	
		We don’t get a lot of detail about what the last three years were like for Sid, because there’s a lot happening in the present. Do you have your own sense of that backstory?	

	I was asking Adam [Randall], the director, a lot about that. We thought that she’d been in a rehabilitation facility that is kept under wraps by MI5. It’s for ex-spies, ex-Joes, and she’s had to learn how to walk and talk again, basically. It’s been an incredibly lonely process that has, I think, cauterized a part of her, in some non-descript location. We were thinking maybe Cumbria, if you know of it. Sort of like the the Vermont of England — very green, but you can get lost in the landscape. I think it’s just been a very long road of recovery, and also of introspection for her.
	
		You mentioned the FOMO earlier, so I’m also interested in what it was like for you to actually step back into the set. I’m sure the non-COVID version of the show feels different.	

	Well, it was pretty much the same crew, and also it’s a lot of the same crew that does “House the Dragon” as well. Like on off seasons with “Slow Horses,” there’ll be people that do dailies and things on “House the Dragon” and vice versa. So I know everyone quite well. It was really lovely. It’s like the best high-school reunion possible. As if you went to a high school and everyone’s your friend, which I don’t think is a reality for anyone. It was just really joyous, even though we shot it right before the December break, in the middle of winter, all night shoots for five weeks, because they truncated all my stuff.



	

									Courtesy of Apple TV
	



	
		I was going to ask about that too — the nocturnal nature of it.	

	I sort of loved it. Adam has this energy about him where it sometimes feels a bit run-and-gun, which I love. And if a particular stunt doesn’t work out, or when we get to the set, the material doesn’t quite match with how the workings of the set are, he’s like, “All right, let’s figure this out. Let’s improvise.” It’s so lovely for me as an actor, too, because I feel like there’s a real energy to that. It did just feel like we were making an independent film for five weeks, because the majority of my stuff was just with Jack and Adam.

	
		Your storyline this season is almost entirely two-handers with Jack. What’s he like as a collaborator?	

	He’s my favorite type of man, which is a very silly man. It’s wonderful acting with him, because he just chucks you a curveball, and then you try and grab it. It makes me feel like I’m stretching my mind in ways that I don’t usually get to do with doing this job. And he’s so fun! He wears it very lightly. He’s such a good actor. He’s very funny, and doesn’t take it too seriously either. Which I love, because sometimes, with other male actors, they take it very serious.
	
		In addition to the night shoots of it all, there’s a lot of action on the show. Were there any particularly tricky sequences?	

	There were, but the one thing that actually did me in was just running. There’s a lot of scenes where I’m just running alongside Jack, who is twice as tall as me, and my 5-foot-5 arse is just desperately trying to keep up. It was like 2 in the morning, and we were being chased by a Land Rover. You’re stretching, you’re trying to keep warm, but I think I’d been a bit static for too long, and we set off and I just felt both thighs go snap. I pulled both of my quad muscles really, really badly. For two weeks, I was hobbling around. Just from a run! But then I thought to myself, “When was the last time I got chased?” Since I was like 12!
	


	
		You’ve gotta have your people page Tom Cruise’s people and be like, “How do I run onscreen?”	



	Literally! Climbing fences, shooting, being on the back of a moving truck while there’s all these fire and gas canisters going off — but just running really, really did me in.
	
		I was curious about the barn interlude. I can’t imagine being in a barn full of smelly cattle for hours on end.	

	The thing is, you can’t really do anything about it. You just have full acceptance 20 minutes in, and get used to it. But we were moving around in and amongst a lot of cows, which was quite scary, actually. They’re really big, and they can kick! I was just remembering old horror stories about people being killed by a stampede of cows, just walking across a field, and I was like, “I’m so close to them!” But it was fine, no one died.
	
		The other action moment that really stood out for me is when you’re on the truck and kicking the oil drum, and it explodes. That looks tricky.	

	That was a crazy, crazy sequence, just trying to dispose of the Russian agents who had come to collect me, and running and jumping on the truck and then Jack just doing donuts around a plane. And you know, Jack does all his own driving stunts! It was very impressive. That was so fun, so cathartic. I love kicking things, and then having this big old stunt where it blows up — it felt like our own Jason Bourne moment.



	

									Courtesy of Apple TV
	


	
		In addition to the action, Sid has a whole emotional trajectory. She seems reluctant for most of the season to accept just how ruthless Diana Taverner has been with her. Why do you think Sid clings to that so much?	

	Because Sid thinks, ultimately, that Diana saved her by getting her out of the hospital, by putting her into some specialized rehab. I think she does genuinely think that she’s only here, she’s only alive because of Diana Taverner. So there’s, I think, some real Stockholm syndrome going on with her. Also, she’s only ever experienced one side of Diana, which has always been very collegial. I think Sid has liked how impressed Diana’s been with her in the past, and hasn’t seen this steely, ruthless side to her that everyone else has experienced.
	
		How do you think she feels once she speaks to Diana on the phone and can’t deny what’s happening anymore?	

	It’s incredibly clarifying, and almost a relief to know that this is the truth — the cold, hard truth. This person thinks that I’m dispensable, that I’m a pawn in whatever game that Diana is trying to play. Knowing that her life could be forfeit so easily — I think through the shock of it — she’s almost giddy. Like, “Oh shit, this is all so obvious to me now.” She kind of has nothing to lose from that point on, because it’s like, “Well, I’m gonna die regardless, going on this plane with these people, so I might as well just try to get out of here.”
	
		You and Jack have great comedic chemistry. But because it’s a spy show, and especially because of what happens at the end of the season, you’re also meant to be questioning everyone’s motivations all the time. Do you have your own read on how Sid feels about River, and how sincere those emotions are?	

	I think despite herself, especially in the first season, her feelings for River have really caught her off guard. I think there’s a genuine connection — this tiny little pinhole of light. River has kept her going, in a sense. Even if they didn’t really get to know each other that well, whatever she’s projected onto River, and the reason why she seeks him out, is because there is something there that has been fizzing for a very, very long time. Especially in the absence. I think those things only get bigger when they’re unresolved, and she’s been so adrift for so long.
	
		I was devastated by the cliffhanger. I can’t believe I have to wait an entire year to find out what happened.	

	I know, I know!
	
	
		Are you someone who reads the books, both to find out what happens with your character and maybe see what happens down the road?	

	In the interim, I hadn’t read the books, but I read for the season that is about to come out, just because I was like, “Surely I’m coming back!” But [Mick Herron] is such a brilliant writer, and he’s so acerbic, and sometimes it’s not faithfully adapted, but they’re really good companions to each other.
	
		Obviously, you can’t tell me anything too specific about the future on the show, but the one thing I was very bummed out by is that we actually don’t get you and Diana face to face in this season. Do we think that might happen in the future?	

	I hope so! I want a showdown. With Kristin Scott Thomas, I think she’s a wonderful actor. I could watch her endlessly. So selfishly, I want that for me, for my dear diary. But yes, it feels like that is a very cathartic thing that must happen.

	
		You’re heading into the final season of “House of the Dragon.” Do you have any goals or plans for the other side of that, when there’s gonna be some free time in your schedule?	

	God, I want to do so much. I really want to do theater. I really, really desperately want to do theater. I am trying. I’ve been trying for years to find the right thing, and maybe I’m just being a bit too picky, and I just need to do it. 

	But theater, and I’d like to be on the other side of the camera a bit more. I’ve been doing this for 14 years now, which doesn’t sound like a lot, but it feels like a lot. And I think I want to find new avenues to go down because I’m getting a bit sick of myself.

	This interview has been edited and condensed.

schema.headline: Olivia Cooke on Returning to ‘Slow Horses,’ On-Set Injuries and That Shocking Finale Cliffhanger: ‘I Want a Showdown!’

title: Anna Marsh on How Canal+ Group’s M&A Activity Helps ‘Challenge the Status Quo’ and Why ‘There’s Just No Room for Error’ in Fast-Moving Business
description: After a busy year that’s seen the Canal+ Group complete a wave of acquisitions across two continents, Anna Marsh, the CEO of Studiocanal and the de
body:
After a busy year that’s seen the Canal+ Group complete a wave of acquisitions across two continents, Anna Marsh, the CEO of Studiocanal and the deputy CEO and chief content officer for Canal+, insisted such moves have been instrumental in strengthening the position of the French media giant at a time of unprecedented industry disruption.

	“It’s really important to have a fresh perspective. People that are going to challenge the status quo. Because the business is moving so fast,” said the New Zealand-born exec, who appeared in conversation at Rome’s MIA Market on Wednesday with MIA head Gaia Tridente.
	

	“The audience is so tough that we constantly need to be looking at ourselves in the mirror. AI is emerging right now. We’ve got enormous consolidation in the U.S. Looking at the different ways that the borders between pay TV and free TV are colliding,” Marsh continued. 


	“There are so many questions to ask. Nobody has all the answers. When we’re able to expand, when we’re able to acquire new companies and enter into new territories, it’s truly enriching.”

	Marsh was speaking in Rome on the heels of GREENLit, MIA’s flagship drama showcase, which offered an exclusive first look at four upcoming international series, among them “Gucci: Game Over,” a six-episode miniseries based on Allegra Gucci’s memoir that’s co-produced by Sky Studios and Lucky Red and distributed internationally by Studiocanal.

	Marsh praised the series as a testament to “the culture, the courage, the history that Europe’s been blessed with,” while insisting to the assembled industry professionals in the room, “I think Europe has a great future when it comes to storytelling. And the depth of the stories that we can tell here is absolutely endless.”
	

	The Canal+ Group acquired a majority stake in Lucky Red, the Rome-based distribution and production company, in February. It was the latest in a series of moves made by the French media conglomerate to expand its growing footprint. Earlier this year, the group acquired a 34-percent stake in UGC, the Paris-headquartered film studio that operates one of France’s leading cinema chains, and also completed a $2 billion takeover of South African pay-TV company MultiChoice.

	That move helped to boost the Canal+ subscriber base to north of 40 million, more than half of whom are English-speaking, thanks to MultiChoice’s reach across the African continent. 

	“That just opens a wealth of opportunity,” said Marsh, who touted recent Canal+ and Studiocanal projects like “The Road Home,” an apartheid-era drama starring Cynthia Erivo, Thabo Rametsi and Guy Pearce which recently wrapped shooting in South Africa, and “Shadow Has Fallen,” a Canal+ original action series, whose third season wrapped in Cape Town.

	“That’s a really strategic part of the group’s focus right now,” she said, of the company’s Africa expansion. “And you can really see how Studiocanal is at the heart of that strategy. If we, as Canal+, enter a new market with so much potential as South Africa, we have to have a strong content strategy.”

	Another pillar in that strategy is Studiocanal Stories, a specialty label launched in 2024 that’s dedicated to book adaptations. Pointing to the blockbuster “Paddington” franchise as the company’s “biggest, most successful IP” to date — and one that “started as a book,” as she noted — Marsh stressed how optioning existing IP “allows us to relax a little bit” because it comes with a built-in audience. 

	“It does give confidence,” she said, “and it does allow us to put more money and more data behind the decision-making.”

	Of course, when it comes to decision-making, some of the old metrics still apply — chief among them talent. That was certainly the case with “What Happens at Night,” an upcoming psychological horror adapted from Peter Cameron’s 2020 novel that’s produced by Apple Studios in partnership with Studiocanal. 

	Directed by Martin Scorsese — “one of the greatest cineastes of all time,” according to Marsh — and starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence, Marsh said the film is as close as one can get in these uncertain times to what she described as “a bit of a slam dunk.”
	

	Still, nothing is guaranteed, with Marsh admitting, “It is harder and harder to hit the bull’s eye.” “Audiences are becoming more and more difficult and their standards are constantly raising,” she said. Especially with Gen Z audiences, “there’s just no room for error.”

	The 12th edition of Rome’s MIA Market runs Oct. 19 – 23.

title: ‘Abbott Elementary’ Season 6 Premiere Hits 6.3 Million Viewers in Seven Days (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The school year is off to a strong start: “Abbott Elementary” returned to ABC with the premiere of its sixth season on Oct. 7 and achieved its stro
body:
The school year is off to a strong start: “Abbott Elementary” returned to ABC with the premiere of its sixth season on Oct. 7 and achieved its strongest viewership in a year.

	After seven days of viewing, the Season 6 premiere reached a total of 6.3 million viewers and a across all platforms. Not only does that represent the show’s best seven-day audience since the third episode of Season 5 on October 15, 2025, one year ago; the episode’s 2.07 rating among adults age 18-49 was the highest in more than 18 months, outpacing all “Abbott” episodes since the 19th episode of Season 4 on March 26, 2025. Compared to the Season 5 premiere in 2025, Season 6 opened with 7% more viewers (up from 5.9 million) and a 16% higher rating (up from 1.79).
	

	Additionally, in terms of streaming specifically, Season 6 premiered with the show’s best seven-day streaming viewership since the ninth episode of Season 4 on Jan. 8, 2025.


	On Oct. 7 alone, the Season 6 premiere brought in 2.2 million viewers and scored a 0.33 rating, meaning that delayed viewing on streaming and other platforms represented increases of 183% and 527%, respectively. 

	“Abbott Elementary” was created by Quinta Brunson, who also leads the cast, while Justin Halpern and Patrick Schumacker serve as showrunners. Executive producers include Brunson; Halpern and Schumacker via their Delicious Non-Sequitur Productions banner; director Randall Einhorn; and writer Brian Rubenstein. Warner Bros. Television and 20th Television serve as co-studios on the comedy series.

title: ‘Glee’ Reboot: Who’s Coming Back? Will Rachel Sing Olivia Rodrigo? How MAGA Is Sue? And More Fan Questions
description:
Oct 21, 2026 3:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘Glee’ Reboot: Who’s Coming Back? Will Rachel Sing Olivia Rodrigo? How MAGA Is Sue? And More Fan Ques
body:
Oct 21, 2026 3:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘Glee’ Reboot: Who’s Coming Back? Will Rachel Sing Olivia Rodrigo? How MAGA Is Sue? And More Fan Questions
	
	
			


			
			
	

									©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection
	

		
	
				

	What have we missed on “Glee”?

	For six glorious, terrifying seasons from 2009 to 2015, we witnessed Ryan Murphy bring a fever dream to life. With each new episode, the musical dramedy series’ unique blend of satire and earnestness had girls, the gays and their allies pondering: What song that should be sung by Mercedes and Santana will get stolen by Rachel next? Why is Mr. Schue so comfortable speaking to children that way? How on earth did any of this get made?

	And now, somehow, the most absurd television project of all time is back. Disney confirmed on Tuesday that Hulu and Disney+ have greenlit a reboot — nay, a Gleeboot — but didn’t provide any details about new storylines or returning cast members. (However, Variety confirmed with multiple sources that at the very least, Lea Michele is set to reprise the role of Rachel Berry.)

	McKinley High School cheer coach Sue Sylvester (played by the inimitable Jane Lynch) once called herself “horny with fear,” and while we won’t go that far… we understand what she meant. So Variety‘s resident gleeks got together and listened to the only version of “Teenage Dream” we recognize to inspire this list of our burning questions about the new “Glee.”


			
			
	What’s the Reboot About?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	Depending on which characters end up returning, there are two semi-obvious (and somewhat non-forced) routes the “Glee” reboot can take. The show ended 11 years ago, so it would totally make sense to center new episodes around William McKinley High School throwing a 10-year reunion that brings back a ton of the original cast. High school culture has changed dramatically in the last decade, so perhaps the reboot finds the original glee club feeling like fish out of water as they contend with rapidly different teenage norms as they meet the school’s current glee club and show them the ropes.

	If only a select number of characters are returning, however, then perhaps the “Glee” reboot centers on Mr. Schue retiring from William McKinley High School. The show ended with Mr. Shue as principal and Sam heading the glee club. Perhaps Mr. Schue’s retirement leads to Sam becoming principal, thus opening the door for (let’s say) Rachel, Kurt and Mercedes to battle it out to be his replacement after their own music careers have sputtered. In this version, you could still have cameos from many original cast members and you’d still meet the new teens who make up the current glee club. The latter point might end up being the biggest no-brainer for the reboot. Whatever the story is, there’s got to be a teenage ensemble/new glee club ready to pick up the mantle and keep the reboot going (and the music sales pumping) for a few years to come.

	But to go off the rails a bit, what if “Glee” returns to a Season 1 storyline? It would be delicious to catch up with Beth, the daughter Quinn and Puck gave up for adoption. Since Beth ended up being raised by Shelby (guest star Idina Menzel), who was not only the coach of McKinley’s rival glee club but also Rachel’s biological mother, the stakes would be high if the reboot follows her show choir journey as she deals with her complex family tree. After all, she should be about 16 years old now…

		
			
			
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	A lot can happen in a decade – and it’s likely that not all our beloved Gleeks will be returning to William McKinley High’s dingy halls. But it seems that Lea Michele wouldn’t miss this opportunity for the world, especially since reviving her career from bullying allegations with rave reviews in “Funny Girl” (just as Rachel Berry would do). Though Disney hasn’t officially confirmed it, Variety has learned from multiple sources that Michele’s return is already guaranteed. Additionally, Heather Morris and Chord Overstreet, who play Brittany Pierce and Sam Evans, have made social media posts that seem to indicate they’ll be back as well.

	For everyone else’s fate, here are our best educated guesses.

	Naturally, Jonathan Groff will make a cameo as Jesse St. James, as he is Michele’s real-life bestie. Darren Criss is probably another sure get, given that he still performs much of Blaine Anderson’s “Glee” material live. Chris Colfer, who played Blaine’s beau Kurt Hummel, said two weeks ago that he’d “heard nothing” about a potential reboot — but then, over the weekend, Colfer and Criss reunited to sing the “Glee” version of “Baby It’s Cold Outside” in London. Coincidence? We think not. Though Colfer has kept quite a low profile since the series, finding success as a bestselling children’s book author instead of pursuing showbiz, now could be the time for him to shimmy back into the spotlight.

	Elsewhere, Harry Shum Jr. (who played Mike Chang), seems to be a lock as he is currently enjoying a renaissance tearing up the dance floor on “Dancing With the Stars” — another Disney-produced show, and perhaps an intentional tie-in. And Matthew Morrison, who has become a TikTok meme with his hilariously earnest cameos, would probably love nothing more than to reprise Mr. Schue.

	We’d say the same of Jane Lynch, though it may depend on the direction of her character – is the political incorrectness of Sue Sylvester too much for these dark times? (More on that later.)

	Speaking of which, Kevin McHale has previously expressed hesitancy to reprise his role of Artie Abrams as he “shouldn’t be playing a character in a wheelchair.” However, as news of a reboot began bubbling up in recent weeks, McHale has appeared more open, telling People: “I could never say no to that.”

	What about Dianna Agron, who played pregnant and slightly evil cheerleader Quinn Fabray? While she hasn’t been very present on TV since “Glee,” Agron is making her return on HBO’s upcoming final season of “Industry.” It again may come down to character direction, as we could see Agron wanting to leave Quinn in the past in favor of more mature roles — and there were rumors back in the day of a feud between her and series creator Murphy.

	Also more uncertain are Amber Riley (Mercedes Jones) and Jenna Ushkowitz (Tina Cohen-Chang). Riley has also kept fairly out of the spotlight and hasn’t publicly spoken about a potential reboot (though we would love to hear her voice again, trust). Ushkowitz still attends “Glee” conventions and speaks about her time on the series, so she seems more likely.

		
			
			
	Where Are the Characters Now?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	If we could get inside that writers’ room (or Ryan Murphy’s head)…

	We imagine Rachel Berry as a washed-up Broadway star who, after a series of scandals, heads back to Ohio in an effort to remember her roots. Jesse St. James left her in the dust at her lowest and cheated on her with his much younger co-star.

	Kurt Hummel and Blaine Anderson are happily married with three kids (their oldest was carried by Rachel, who they see as an aunt). They run a LBGTQ+ arts nonprofit in New York City and also have a home upstate in Hudson.

	Will Schuester is still the principal at McKinley High, but after a decade of being in charge, the job has hardened him. He barely sings anymore and is pretty miserable.

	Sue Sylvester was a close-second to be the Republican candidate for the 2024 election, but lost out to Trump. Now, she’s his chief of staff. The two have been having a hate-fueled affair for years.

	Quinn Fabray is a high-powered lawyer living in L.A. with her husband and two young kids. She hasn’t been back to Ohio in 10 years.

	Mercedes Jones has achieved EGOT status and is besties with Beyoncé. Whenever her tours stop in Ohio, she visits McKinley High School and has never forgotten where she came from.

	Tina Cohen-Chang is a respected theater actress in New York, where she runs her own improv group. She’s rekindled things with Mike Chang, who is now a Broadway choreographer, after they worked on a show together.

	Brittany Pierce is a math teacher and cheer coach at McKinley. She’s a devoted mother to her and Santana’s two daughters, who are of course, Cheerios.

	Sam Evans is still coaching New Directions at McKinley High, having led them to 10 consecutive state championships. But he’s at a crossroads after finally being offered a record deal of his own in Nashville.

	And when it comes to Artie Abrams… where do we begin? He probably sold out and directed a few Marvel movies that flopped — or maybe they were DC movies, since Disney likely wouldn’t be happy with Murphy for making fun of its most popular franchise. Artie and Tina didn’t work out, but he’s trying to win her back by directing a movie musical inspired by their time in Glee club.

	As we mentioned above, McHale has said before that he shouldn’t be playing a disabled character. He’s right, but is that really the problem? The simple fact of McHale’s casting was far less problematic than the fact that he once rolled himself straight into a swimming pool for a split-second gag during the glee club’s cover of Rihanna’s “We Found Love.” It would be even more offensive to pretend Artie’s spinal cord injury could be magically healed, allowing Abrams to play him as able-bodied… but it would be very “Glee.”

		
			
			
	How MAGA Has Sue Sylvester Become?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	Jane Lynch said it herself in a 2022 interview with the Guardian: Sue Sylvester “would be MAGA” should “Glee” ever return. After all, the hugely problematic, tracksuit-loving cheerleading coach ended the show in the White House as the Republican Vice President of the United States with plans to run for the top job. “Glee” wrapped up about a year before Donald Trump took office, so perhaps part of the reboot will dive head first into how Sue’s political goals and the Trump administration merged into one toxic whole. Maybe Sue went head to head against Trump in an election? Just imagine that presidential debate for a second. Or maybe Sue is a member of the Trump administration and the only thing that can force her to rebuke her MAGA ways is the power of a good song. Yes, Sue embraced the Glee club (even as a Republican) come the end of the show, but something tells us right-wing Facebook groups would’ve swallowed her whole during the rise of Trump and send her right back to her sexist, homophobic roots.

	In the same Guardian interview, Lynch said: “I think there would have been people out there who would have wanted to cancel Sue Sylvester” if the show was airing today. If Lynch is in fact returning to her Emmy-winning role for the reboot, then fans can probably expect MAGA Sue confronting 2026 “woke” culture to be a defining subplot.

		
			
			
	What Songs Will They Cover?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	In the decade since “Glee” left the air, musings about which current pop hits would have been used on “Glee” have practically become their own subgenre of social media post. When “This Is America” dropped in 2018, X (then still called Twitter) was full of posts thanking God that Artie Abrams wasn’t around to rap Childish Gambino’s bars; the gleeks of West Hollywood have mourned that Kurt Hummel never got to hear Chappell Roan’s “Pink Pony Club”; et cetera. Now that the reboot is official, everything’s on the table. 

	Olivia Rodrigo would be the most obvious artist to include in the lineup of new “Glee” music. Her pop-punk flair is right up the glee club’s alley, and she even referenced the show in the lyrics of her 2021 single “Deja Vu.” “Drivers License” would be an on-the-nose pick for one of the new high schoolers, while “Stupid Song” is very Rachel Berry. And can’t you see Brittany and Mike doing backflips to a full-cast cover of “Expectations”?

	Plus, Rodrigo is already friendly with Disney, having launched her career on “High School Musical: The Musical: The Series.” The same is true of Sabrina Carpenter, who got her start on “Girl Meets World,” and we can totally see Kurt and Blaine working through a trivial lover’s spat with a sunny rendition of “Manchild.”

	From “Wicked” to “Funny Girl” to “Rent,” “Glee” covered its fair share of showtunes in its day, but it ended too early to see the rise of “Hamilton.” Rachel, obsessed with Broadway, surely would have pined over the role of Angelica Schuyler and sung “Satisfied” if she could have — and especially since Disney is already home to the filmed version of the musical, that now seems likely. Perhaps an entire Lin-Manuel Miranda-themed episode to appease to the musical theater nerds? We’re cringing, but we can’t wait. 

	Mercedes was a Beyoncé devotee from the beginning of “Glee” to the end, when she was picked to be the icon’s opening act on tour. Between “Lemonade,” “Renaissance” and “Cowboy Carter,” there’s an embarrassment of riches to choose from. We’d love to see her get a meaty romantic plotline that peaks with a cover of “Heated,” complete with vogueing glee club members in the background.

	And yes, “Pink Pony Club” should absolutely be a Kurt solo. At the same time, it would be the most “Glee” move in the world for Rachel to fight him over it à la “Defying Gravity” in Season 1.

		
			
			
	How Will Deaths in the Cast Be Addressed?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	Three of the “Glee” cast members have passed away: Cory Monteith in 2013, Mark Salling in 2018 and Naya Rivera in 2020.

	Monteith died from an overdose while the original “Glee” was still on the air, so he already got a substantial tribute: The Season 5 episode “The Quarterback” showed all of the glee club members who had graduated returning to Ohio to mourn together, including moving covers of songs like “Seasons of Love.” Out of sensitivity, there was no cause of death specified for Monteith’s character, Finn, but the episode concluded with a PSA encouraging viewers to seek help for mental health and substance abuse issues. Overall, it was handled with sensitivity and care. And since the “Glee” reboot will be full of nostalgia, and we can be sure that Rachel and other characters will reference fond (and funny) memories of Finn when they reunite.

	Rivera played the bitchy-yet-lovable cheerleader Santana, a fan-favorite character who was widely mourned when Rivera died in a drowning accident. Many fans returned to her heartbreaking (and now eerie) cover of “If I Die Young” from Monteith’s tribute episode after she died. Santana’s girlfriend (and later wife) Brittany, played by Heather Morris, may think back to that moment as well. And some of the most popular “Glee” covers ever were sung by Santana and Mercedes, so perhaps Amber Riley will dedicate a song to her departed friend.

	Salling’s death is where things get complicated. Unlike Monteith and Rivera, whose deaths led to celebrations of their legacies, Salling was mired in controversy: He was arrested for possession of child pornography months after “Glee” ended, pleaded guilty in 2017 and died by suicide a year later. But his character, the secretly sensitive bad boy Puck, was one of the most important characters on the show. So how does “Glee” forward? While we’re thrilled about the reboot, the problem of Puck is one aspect we’re truly dreading.

	The sensible option would to include a brief, throwaway line about Puck being dead or somewhere far away while catching up with one of the other characters — perhaps Puck’s half-brother Jake, played by Jacob Artist.  But, outside of the Monteith tribute, when has “Glee” ever been sensible?

		
			
			
	How Will ‘Glee’ Change on Streaming?
			
										
					Image Credit: ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection				
					
				

	As crazy as “Glee” was, it still had to abide by the strict guidelines imposed on network television. Airing on Fox meant there was a limit on the adult language, imagery and themes Murphy and his collaborators could show.

	But since “Glee” is heading straight to Hulu and Disney+, all bets are off. The characters will be allowed to use any curse words they’d like, and the floor is open for more graphic sex scenes. Mr. Schue’s rendition of “The Thong Song” was already horrifying on broadcast. Can you imagine how far he might have taken it on streaming? We don’t even want to think about how the Season 5 cover of “Blurred Lines” — in which the glee club protests a school-wide ban on twerking — might have looked without the looming threat of FCC regulations.

	“Glee” was never very violent, but it might have gone further in that direction on streaming. Take the infamous school shooting episode in Season 4, for example, which was already completely unhinged without anyone getting hurt. With the original “Glee” cast now in their 30s and dealing with real adult problems, there’s a whole new world of darkness the show might now begin to explore. 

		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: ‘Glee’ Reboot: Who’s Coming Back? Will Rachel Sing Olivia Rodrigo? How MAGA Is Sue? And More Fan Questions

title: Jeffrey Epstein's Former Lawyer And Accountant Accused by New Mexico AG Of Covering Up Sex Trafficking Ring
description:
Jeffrey Epstein
                          Estate Executors Reportedly Accused by New Mexico AG of
body:
Jeffrey Epstein
                          Estate Executors Reportedly Accused by New Mexico AG of Sex Trafficking Cover-Up
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 21, 2026
                            1:06 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jeffrey Epstein's former attorney and accountant have been dragged to court by the New Mexico Attorney General and accused of covering up a sex trafficking ring at the late financier's Zorro Ranch near Santa Fe.
      
    
            The allegations were made in a lawsuit -- filed Wednesday -- that aims to prevent attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn from receiving payments from Epstein's massive estate ... AP News reported.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            While the estate's co-executors have previously maintained their ignorance of Epstein's crimes ... New Mexico AG Raúl Torrez said ... "None of this could be done by just one man. This was something that was facilitated, that was made possible by handlers, by lawyers, by accountants, by others who have yet to face real consequences."
      

            Torrez added that the vast funds of Epstein's estate "belong in the hands of survivors."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We reported last month ... the FBI had begun investigating Indyke and Kahn, with their attorney, Daniel Ruzumna, confirming the probe.
      
    
            At the time ... Ruzumna said that despite the inquiry, Indyke and Kahn -- who are also named as co-defendants in a lawsuit filed by a Jane Doe against Epstein's estate -- had not been implicated in probes back in 2018 and 2019.
      
    
            We reached out to Ruzumna for comment ... so far, no word back.

Olivier Martinez
                          It's Not 'Storming Out' If Nature Calls

                                                                        Published 
                              October 21, 2026

            Olivier Martinez is pleased with the court proceedings, at least so far, in his domestic violence dispute with Halle Berry, so his lawyer says there's no reason he'd angrily race out of court.
      
    
            Olivier's attorney Patrick Baghdaserians tells TMZ ... the report he and his client stormed out of the courtroom during Tuesday's testimony is false, and they'd simply requested a bathroom break. He says the judge granted them 3 minutes to step out, and they wasted no time.
      
    
            Baghdaserians also shot down claims they might have been unhappy with the testimony that day, telling us Olivier is happy with how the case is currently unfolding.
      
    
            Martinez and Berry are now on day 3 of testimony in their domestic dispute case, with their 13-year-old son, Maceo -- who is at the center of the claims -- testifying for the majority of Monday, before the head of his school, John Hay, took the stand.
      
    
            Halle continued to testify today, and Olivier took the stand towards the end of the day. Halle has called on her boyfriend Van Hunt and daughter Nahla Aubry to speak in her favor.
      
    
            We're told Nahla will appear virtually for her testimony.

title: Harry Styles Goes Off On Man Asking for Autograph on NYC Street
description:
Harry Styles
                          Heated Exchange with Man in NYC
body:
Harry Styles
                          Heated Exchange with Man in NYC
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 21, 2026
                            2:28 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 21, 2026
                                3:46 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Harry Styles got into it with a man in NYC who wanted an autograph ... and from the looks of it, he was heated.
      
    
            TMZ obtained video of Harry from Wednesday, having an animated interaction with a man who was holding his "Fine Line" album ... although it's unclear what exactly set the guys off.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            At one point, you can see a third man step in between Harry and the autograph seeker, trying to diffuse the tension.
      

            And when Harry eventually tries to walk off, the man follows, matching Harry's stride.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            There's also another clip of the man walking down the street alongside Harry, seemingly trying to get his attention -- but HS clearly wasn't having it.
      
    
            It's unlike Harry to deny fans an autograph as he recently stopped in his tracks at the Knicks game last night ... when he gave his autograph to a lucky fan before heading into the arena.

            According to the citation, obtained by TMZ, the "Laguna Beach" alum was stopped by the cop on October 14 while driving around in a black Porsche 911.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The reality star was cited for speeding … allegedly going 88 mph in a 70 mph zone.
      

            Per the report, the police officer saw Kristin speeding on the highway in the number one lane and passing another vehicle.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            During their conversation, the officer says Kristin told him she was on her way to her business. It's worth noting the reality star has a store for her clothing brand, Uncommon James, in the city.
      
    
            Kristin has been living in Tennessee for over a decade since moving to the state with her now ex-husband, Jay Cutler.
      
    
            Talk about living life in the fast lane!
